title: Facet
description: A dimension. Kind generalised: open-ended rather than closed, hierarchical rather than flat, multi-valued rather than single, and able to classify anything addressable as a subject. This schema describes the YAML front matter of one file under knowledge/facets/ or knowledge/meta/. The prose body of that file is not described here and is not optional: it says what the facet is for and, more importantly, what does not belong on it.

id.description: Stable identifier. Also addressable as the subject 'facet:<id>', which is how a facet is classified by another facet.

version.description: Semantic version of this facet's own definition, independent of the repository version.

kind.description: hierarchical: paths nest and a parent implies its children. categorical: a flat closed-ish set. scalar: paths carry an ordered value. boolean: presence or absence.

separator.description: Segment separator for paths on this facet. Declared per facet rather than assumed, because a facet borrowed from another vocabulary may not use a colon.

paths.description: Every path this facet currently defines. A path removed from this list without an alias somewhere is a broken promise; see NAMING.md.

supersedes.description: Facet ids this one replaced, by merge or rename. Empty for a facet that has never changed identity.

meta.description: True when this facet classifies facets rather than ordinary subjects. Such a file lives in knowledge/meta/. This is the recursion and it is load-bearing: a facet measuring evidence quality applies to facets themselves.

path.description: The full path, including every ancestor segment. Written out rather than implied by nesting so that a line of this file is meaningful on its own.

aliases.description: Names that also resolve to this path. A rename never deletes: the old name lands here. See NAMING.md.

since.description: Facet version in which this path first resolved.

description.description: One line. What belongs here and what does not.

deprecated.description: Set when the path still resolves but should not be assigned to new subjects. It is never simply removed.
